name: Robert Garcia

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TESTIMONY OF MARIA FARMER, "SURVIVORS FIGHT FOR JUSTICE: EXPOSING EPSTEIN'S CRIMES IN PALM BEACH AND ACROSS THE WORLD"
statements.title: TESTIMONY OF MARIA FARMER, "SURVIVORS FIGHT FOR JUSTICE: EXPOSING EPSTEIN'S CRIMES IN PALM BEACH AND ACROSS THE WORLD"
sentences: Mr. Speaker, on May 12, 2026, Oversight Committee Democrats convened the first-ever hearing to solicit testimony from survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell's crimes.
The hearing, ``Survivors Fight for Justice: Exposing Epstein's Crimes in Palm Beach and Across the World,'' marked a critical step forward in the fight for justice and accountability.
On behalf of all the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell's crimes, I rise to include in the Record the testimony offered by Ms. Maria Farmer: My name is Maria Farmer.
I am the whistleblower who reported Jeffrey Epstein, Ghislaine Maxwell, Les Wexner, and others to the FBI 30 years ago in 1996.
In 1996, I reported Epstein and his co-conspirators to my local New York City Sixth Precinct.
The Commanding Officer told me local police could only address the local arson crimes, and he instructed me to immediately report the whole story, spanning several states, to the FBI.

That failure-- that single moment when law enforcement refused to take action--set off a cascade of injustice and grave repercussions to my sisters, my family, and so many others, and to me personally, including my health and well-being.
In 2006, the FBI tracked me down, stating that they searched for me because they knew I had reported Epstein ten years earlier and no one else had.
They urged me to testify in a federal criminal trial against Epstein and his co- conspirators, and they promised that they would ``get him'' this time.

Rather than following through with their promises, the government offered Epstein a sweetheart deal and shielded powerful individuals from accountability, and they persist in granting special treatment to certain people to this day.

With the passage of the Epstein Files Transparency Act, after years of efforts to get my records, an FD-71 form was released for the first time, confirming part of my 1996 whistleblower report and vindicating some of what I had said for years.
However, the full extent of what I told the FBI was not in that document, so the release of the Epstein Files provides only partial relief for me.
As the Epstein case whistleblower, I have waited three decades for justice.
I will keep fighting for justice and transparency, for a better, safer future for the next generation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISAPPROVING THE ACTION OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA COUNCIL IN APPROVING THE D.C. INCOME AND FRANCHISE TAX CONFORMITY AND REVISION TEMPORARY AMENDMENT ACT OF 2025
statements.title: DISAPPROVING THE ACTION OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA COUNCIL IN APPROVING THE D.C. INCOME AND FRANCHISE TAX CONFORMITY AND REVISION TEMPORARY AMENDMENT ACT OF 2025
sentences: The DOJ is defying the law to withhold the Epstein files.
Mr. Speaker, I also strongly oppose this resolution, which is yet another attack on the rights of over 700,000 D.C. residents.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to oppose H.J. Res. 142.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECT AMERICA'S WORKFORCE ACT
statements.title: PROTECT AMERICA'S WORKFORCE ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong support of the Protecting America's Workforce Act, which will restore collective bargaining rights for more than 1 million Federal workers.
In March, President Trump signed an executive order terminating collective bargaining rights for Federal police officers, firefighters, nurses, food safety inspectors, and so many more.
The nurses who care for our veterans, the flight safety inspectors at the FAA, nuclear power plant safety workers, and countless others lost their right to have representation in the workplace.
Workers deserve the right to make their voices heard with a union.
I am so proud to partner with our city unions, always making sure that the city and services ran effectively.
Our Federal unions are the same.
President Trump is targeting Federal unions to further his power grab and to continue to push an agenda which leaves working families behind and, instead, supports billionaires.
Unions make our middle class stronger.
We should be working every day to strengthen the right to organize and not to undermine it.

We are talking about our Federal nurses, our firefighters, law enforcement, medical professionals, the men and women who are working across our airports, that are taking care of our nuclear reactors in this country.
They deserve the right to organize.
We should be fighting to provide world-class government services, and we should be fighting for the unions which make all that possible.
We should be working hard to expand the right to organize, not turning back the clock on working families.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA CASH BAIL REFORM ACT OF 2025
statements.title: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA CASH BAIL REFORM ACT OF 2025
sentences: If Republicans want to get tough on crime, they should stop protecting the criminals in the Epstein files and demand transparency from Donald Trump.
It will reinforce an unfair system where the rich get perks, while the poor suffer.
Democrats are fighting for a system where wealthy elites aren't above the law but where the justice system is fair for all.
Mr. Speaker, I strongly oppose the legislation which is in front of us, which is another completely unacceptable attack on the District and on democratic principles.
We are fighting for democracy.
I urge my colleagues to oppose it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: COMMON-SENSE LAW ENFORCEMENT AND ACCOUNTABILITY NOW IN DC ACT OF 2025
statements.title: COMMON-SENSE LAW ENFORCEMENT AND ACCOUNTABILITY NOW IN DC ACT OF 2025
sentences: They empower the chief of police to lead the police department and do it the right way.
It would damage the trust between D.C. police and the communities they protect and serve.
We know communities are safer when residents feel safe calling on 911 and when they feel safe working with the police.
We know policies like de-escalation, expanding body-worn cameras, and improving safety should not move backwards.
This bill undermines trust between police and the community they serve and makes us all less safe.
Again, I strongly oppose this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EPSTEIN FILES TRANSPARENCY ACT
statements.title: EPSTEIN FILES TRANSPARENCY ACT
sentences: We know that Donald Trump has tried everything to kill our Jeffrey Epstein investigation.
He is about to lose this Epstein vote to force the Department of Justice to release the files.
Why won't they release the Epstein files right now?
We should get justice for the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein.
Next steps are the bank and financial records to follow and expose Epstein's network.
Today, there should be a unanimous vote on releasing the files, and we will get justice.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA JUDICIAL NOMINATIONS REFORM ACT
statements.title: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA JUDICIAL NOMINATIONS REFORM ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I strongly oppose this bill, which would eliminate the D.C. Judicial Nomination Commission and give a President, any President, the sole power to make nominations for D.C. local courts, which deal with municipal issues.
Mr. Speaker, I just will clarify for the gentleman from Texas that these are not Federal circuit judges.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA POLICING PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA POLICING PROTECTION ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I strongly oppose this bill, which would overrule rules implemented by D.C.'s elected leaders on when Metropolitan Police officers should pursue a fleeing car.
Over 3,000 people died in police car chases in the U.S. between 2017 and 2022.
Half of the people who have died in police car chases were innocent bystanders.
Congress should not require D.C. police to use tactics that the community does not want.
D.C. residents should be empowered to decide when to authorize their police to use dangerous tactics.
There are many tools, we know, that police officers can use to track suspects and make arrests.
We should let the Council, the Mayor, and the police work together with the D.C. police to balance public safety, pedestrian safety, and proportionality.

Today, Congress is again injecting itself as some sort of super city council to write laws for Washington, D.C. As a former mayor of 8 years, I worked with over 700 amazing men and women of a police department who were heroic in the work that they did.

I know that, in conversations with our chief, our police officers, and our community, these decisions are best left to our communities to write the laws of when these police chases should actually go into effect.
Mr. Speaker, I thank the gentleman from Louisiana (Mr. Higgins) also for his service in law enforcement.
I will remind us that this District is dense.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DC CRIMINAL REFORMS TO IMMEDIATELY MAKE EVERYONE SAFE ACT
statements.title: DC CRIMINAL REFORMS TO IMMEDIATELY MAKE EVERYONE SAFE ACT
sentences: It eliminates a judge's ability to waive mandatory minimums, even when the facts show a one-size-fits-all sentence makes no sense.
Now, we also know that in nearly 80 percent of cases, judges impose a mandatory minimum sentence anyway.
Now, Republicans in the majority claim D.C.'s policies are too soft, but we know that the sponsor of this bill is also from Florida, which has allowed judges to waive mandatory minimums for decades.
We know what works: supporting local police departments, investing in community-based partnerships, and creating economic opportunity to drive down shootings, homicides, and burglaries.
Trump has opposed efforts to expand criminal background checks.
He has blocked attempts to reduce ghost guns and machine gun conversion devices.

On top of that, Trump illegally froze or canceled $3.8 billion in DOJ grant programs, including COPS grants for our police departments that, of course, help communities hire and train police officers.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LOWERING AGE AT WHICH A MINOR MAY BE TRIED AS ADULT FOR CERTAIN CRIMINAL OFFENSES IN DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA
statements.title: LOWERING AGE AT WHICH A MINOR MAY BE TRIED AS ADULT FOR CERTAIN CRIMINAL OFFENSES IN DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA
sentences: Instead of taking power away from D.C. residents and our elected officials, Congress should focus on real national priorities like addressing gun violence that threatens communities, threatens schools, and threatens our cities every single day.

I remind my colleagues that at this moment, what we are doing right now, is stripping 700,000 residents who have come together in D.C. to create laws, to bring community together, to fight for statehood and representation, we are going to strip them from their ability to manage their own city.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RELEASE THE EPSTEIN FILES
statements.title: RELEASE THE EPSTEIN FILES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to demand that Donald Trump and our Attorney General come clean to the American people and release the Epstein files.
Now, this weekend, Donald Trump said: ``Let's . . . not waste time and energy on Jeffrey Epstein, somebody that nobody cares about.'' Well, Mr. President, a lot of people actually care.
We know that MAGA was all in on Jeffrey Epstein.
FBI Director Kash Patel swore under oath in front of the Senate that he would be transparent with the American public and release the Epstein files.
Now, in February, Attorney General Pam Bondi told FOX News that Epstein's client list is: ``Sitting on my desk right now to review.'' Now, they claim there was never a list.
We know Elon Musk said publicly on June 5 that Donald Trump is mentioned in the Epstein files.
We know that Epstein died in a Federal prison overseen by Donald Trump's Department of Justice.
We know that Jeffrey Epstein in 2008 was given a generous nonprosecution agreement for sex trafficking charges.
We know that Donald Trump and Epstein had a longstanding personal relationship.
Epstein told one writer: ``I was Donald Trump's closest friend for 10 years.'' Donald Trump told New York magazine in 2002: ``I've known Jeff for 15 years.
I can't explain why the Trump administration has changed their minds on Epstein, but their behavior raises questions.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, my Democratic colleagues and I believe in a country where we take care of our fellow Americans and the wealthiest pay their fair share.
It is a transfer from the poor and the middle class to the wealthiest.
It does all of this while increasing debt over $3 trillion.
What happened to fiscal responsibility?
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no'' on this big BS bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONDEMNING THE ATTACKS ON MINNESOTA LAWMAKERS IN BROOKLYN PARK AND CHAMPLIN, MINNESOTA, AND CALLING FOR UNITY AND THE REJECTION OF POLITICAL VIOLENCE IN MINNESOTA A
statements.title: CONDEMNING THE ATTACKS ON MINNESOTA LAWMAKERS IN BROOKLYN PARK AND CHAMPLIN, MINNESOTA, AND CALLING FOR UNITY AND THE REJECTION OF POLITICAL VIOLENCE IN MINNESOTA AND ACROSS THE UNITED STATES
sentences: I want to take this time to thank State, Federal, and local law enforcement for their tireless work to bring the perpetrator to justice.
It is important that we continue to push back against hate, fear, division, and misinformation in a bipartisan way.
Mr. Speaker, I urge the adoption of the resolution, and I yield back the balance of my time.
Today, we will come together in a bipartisan way to condemn these senseless attacks and reject political violence.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GERALD E. CONNOLLY ESOPHAGEAL CANCER AWARENESS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: GERALD E. CONNOLLY ESOPHAGEAL CANCER AWARENESS ACT OF 2025
sentences: He served as a county executive where he fought to expand affordable housing and to invest in infrastructure, and he always supported public workers.
Mr. Speaker, I strongly support this bill, which of course, supports our fight against cancer and to improve healthcare for all Federal workers.
Now, Gerry represented the best among us in public service, which is why we strongly support this bill.
Mr. Speaker, I urge every Member to honor Gerry by supporting this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GROSS VIOLATIONS OF LAW BY TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
statements.title: GROSS VIOLATIONS OF LAW BY TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
sentences: Yet, Donald Trump, of course, thinks he is above the law.
Mr. Speaker, that is why I have introduced the Hatch Act Enforcement Transparency and Accountability Act earlier this year.
If the Trump administration or anyone else in power refuses to investigate a clear violation, we will know why, and we will demand accountability.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICIES
statements.title: TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICIES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, there is no issue right now that should concern Americans more than the elimination and destruction of due process, not just now for U.S. citizens but for people who are here whether it is a legal status or because they have been invited to this country to apply for asylum.
He is a gay hairstylist and makeup artist who came to the United States with an asylum appointment.
The United States Government gave Andry an appointment to show up to the border so that he could claim asylum using our process that we created.

His initial screening is positive, and then he essentially gets taken at the border from that screening directly to a prison in El Salvador, a country he knows nothing about, in a process that eliminated his right through the court and due process asylum system that we have created in this country.
What kind of America is this where we are doing this to people who are seeking asylum?
Yes, he has a crown tattoo reflective of a festival back in his home city and state in Venezuela.

Because an ICE agent, who was, by the way, a disgraced former police officer, made these claims, Andry is now in a foreign prison, and his family and his lawyers have not heard anything about him in weeks.
I did go to El Salvador to advocate for the release of not just Kilmar, who has been mandated by the Supreme Court to come back, but also for Andry.
